chunk_findings.detail: `session.cancelled` is never cleared, so a cancel becomes sticky for the whole session lifetime. After any `session/cancel` for a session, the next `session/prompt` on that same session still sees `session.cancelled=True`; `_prompt` calls `self._on_prompt` (so side effects can happen) and then returns `{"stopReason": "cancelled"}` regardless of the real stop reason. For example: initialize, `session/new` returns `s1`, send `{"method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":"s1"}}` while no prompt is active (or cancel a first prompt), then send `session/prompt` for `s1` with an `on_prompt` that returns `"end_turn"`. The adapter returns stopReason `"cancelled"`, so the session is permanently treated as cancelled for later prompts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The `session/cancel` branch is executed before any mapping validation and before `check_request`, and it calls `params.get` / `self.sessions.get` unguarded. A JSON-RPC message with array `params` crashes the handler: `handle({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/cancel","params":["s1"]})` makes `params` a non-empty list, so `params.get(...)` raises `AttributeError`. Likewise, `handle({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":[]}})` raises `TypeError` from `self.sessions.get([])`. Since `session/cancel` is a notification, malformed params should be ignored (or, if it carried an id, answered as invalid params), not raised.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent.handle

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpAgent.handle` treats `session/cancel` as safe for any JSON value in `sessionId`. Given a malformed but parseable notification such as `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId": []}}`, line 47 calls `self.sessions.get([])`, which raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. The same handler guards `session/prompt` with `isinstance(sid, str)` (line 75), so a bad cancel notification should not crash the fake agent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:47

chunk_findings.detail: The fake agent never clears `session.cancelled` after a prompt completes. With the default `Script(stop_reason="end_turn")`, a client can do `connect()`, `new_session()`, `cancel(session_id)`, then `prompt(session_id, "first")` and get `A.CANCELLED`; a second `prompt(session_id, "second")` on the same session also returns `A.CANCELLED` because line 81 still sees the sticky `session.cancelled` flag. This makes a session permanently cancelled even though the scripted stop reason is supposed to be replayed for each new prompt.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:81

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpAgent` ignores `Script.asks` when acting as the agent half. For example, `Script(asks=[{"toolCall": {"title": "edit"}}])`; if the agent is driven through `serve` or direct `handle` calls for `initialize`, `session/new`, and `session/prompt`, `agent.sent` contains only `session/update` notifications and JSON-RPC replies, never any permission ask. The module and `Script` docstrings state that the fake agent replays permission asks on every prompt, so the agent-side fake does not implement its scripted ask behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:78

chunk_findings.detail: `_Peer` stores the pending prompt request id in `self.asking`, but later tests it as a boolean (`if "method" not in msg and self.asking:`). If the client uses a legal JSON-RPC id of `0` (or `null`) for `session/prompt`, `self.asking` becomes falsy, so when the client sends the answer to `session/request_permission` the answer branch is skipped; `_Peer` then never emits the prompt response and `client.prompt` hangs until timeout. The conformance case assumes request ids are always truthy.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:_Peer.send

chunk_findings.detail: The `session/request_permission` response is double-wrapped. `outcome` is already the ACP result object (`{"outcome": "selected", "optionId": chosen}` or `{"outcome": "cancelled"}`), but the code calls `ok(msg["id"], {"outcome": outcome})`. A conforming agent therefore receives `"result": {"outcome": {"outcome": "selected", ...}}` instead of `"result": {"outcome": "selected", ...}`. When the agent requests permission, it cannot parse the response and the prompt fails or hangs. [D-acp-r2]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._on_other

chunk_findings.detail: `session/cancel` cannot cancel a running prompt. `serve` feeds one line at a time to `handle`, and `handle("session/prompt")` blocks inside `_on_prompt` until the turn returns. A `session/cancel` frame sent while the turn is running is not read, so the `session.cancelled = True` code never executes during the active prompt. An on_prompt that runs until cancellation, as the OnPrompt contract describes, deadlocks instead of stopping. [D-acp-r2]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent

chunk_findings.detail: `session.cancelled` is set by any `session/cancel` and is never reset at the start of the next `session/prompt`. After a session has been cancelled once — even when no prompt was active — every later prompt on that session returns `"cancelled"` regardless of the stop reason produced by `_on_prompt`. Input: create a session, send `session/cancel`, then `session/prompt` with `_on_prompt` returning `"end_turn"`; the response is `{"stopReason": "cancelled"}`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `Script.asks` are never emitted by `FakeAcpAgent.handle`; they only appear because `FakeAcpClient.prompt` reaches directly into `self.agent.script.asks` and synthesizes `result.permissions` after the prompt response has already returned. That contradicts the module doc’s claim that `FakeAcpAgent` replays the scripted permission asks, and it means any Server-half test, or any direct use of `FakeAcpAgent`, never sees a permission-ask message from the agent. For example, after creating a session and sending `session/prompt` with `Script(asks=[{"toolCall": {"title": "save"}}])`, `agent.sent` contains only `session/update` notifications and no permission ask, so the fake does not exercise the ACP permission-request path the real adapter must handle.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py FakeAcpAgent.handle / FakeAcpClient.prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `_exchange` fails to handle JSON-RPC error responses returned by the ACP agent. When the agent responds with an `error` object instead of a `result`, the check `if "result" in msg:` at line 441 evaluates to `False`, causing the subsequent line `return done(ERROR, error=msg["error"] ...)` to crash with a `KeyError: 'error'` if the response dictionary `msg` lacks the `"error"` key, or to incorrectly handle valid JSON-RPC error frames that contain an error object. Given a JSON-RPC response input lacking an `"error"` key (e.g., `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1}`), line 441 raises an unhandled `KeyError` and aborts the client request.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:441

chunk_findings.detail: `session.cancelled` is a single session-wide flag with no association to the prompt turn that is currently running. If a `session/cancel` notification arrives while no prompt is active, or arrives just after a previous prompt has already been answered, `handle` still sets `session.cancelled = True`. The next `session/prompt` call then runs `on_prompt` (line 254) and afterwards returns `stopReason: "cancelled"` (lines 255-256), even though the cancel was not for that turn. Example: `initialize`, `session/new`, a `session/cancel` notification for that session, then `session/prompt`; the prompt side effects run and the response is `cancelled`, which is wrong because a cancel for an idle/completed turn should not cancel the next turn.
chunk_findings.title: AcpStdioAgent._prompt (ddflow/adapters/acp.py:206-210, 254-256)

chunk_findings.detail: The `session/cancel` branch returns `None` before the adapter checks whether the incoming message is a JSON-RPC request. A message with an `id` is a request and must receive a response. Given `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":"s1"}}`, `handle` marks the session cancelled if the id is known and returns `None`; the caller can wait forever for a response. It should return an error/refusal response for a request-shaped cancel, not silence.
chunk_findings.title: AcpStdioAgent.handle (ddflow/adapters/acp.py:206-210)

chunk_findings.detail: Permission handling assumes `params["toolCall"]` is dict-like whenever it is truthy. Given an agent request such as `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"session/request_permission","params":{"toolCall":"bad"}}`, line 409 evaluates `("bad" or {}).get("title", "")` and raises `AttributeError`. With no policy, the intended behavior is to refuse the permission request; instead `prompt()` aborts with an exception and returns no `PromptResult`.
chunk_findings.title: AcpStdioClient._on_other (ddflow/adapters/acp.py:406-414)

chunk_findings.detail: The server accepts Python booleans as protocol versions because `True == 1`. Given `{"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":true}}`, line 218 returns `protocolVersion: true` in the JSON response. That is not an integer protocol version, and the client-side `negotiate_version` explicitly treats boolean answers as “no usable answer” (line 104), so this response becomes an unknown handshake fact instead of a valid/supported fact.
chunk_findings.title: AcpStdioAgent.handle (ddflow/adapters/acp.py:217-218)

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpClient.prompt` dereferences `out.result` before checking `out.status`. Given a connected client and session, calling `prompt("missing", "hi", 1.0)` makes `FakeAcpAgent.handle` return a JSON-RPC error for the unknown session, `_ask` returns an `A.Outcome` with status `A.ERROR` and `result=None`, and line 163 raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` instead of returning a `PromptResult` carrying the error status. The same pattern at line 146 in `new_session` crashes on an agent error (for example `new_session(None, [], 1.0)`), so the fake does not “answer” like the real port adapter [D-adapters-answers].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:163

chunk_findings.detail: A cancel notification that arrives after a completed turn is treated as a cancel of the next turn. With a connected client and session, `prompt(...)` returns `end_turn`; then `cancel(session_id)` sets `session.cancelled=True`; the next `prompt(...)` reads that flag at line 83 and returns `stop_reason=A.CANCELLED`, even though the cancel was sent after the previous turn had already ended. The comment says a cancel ends one turn, but in this synchronous fake it arms the *following* prompt instead of affecting only the turn in flight.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:83

chunk_findings.detail: `session/cancel` is broken by the synchronous read loop. `AcpStdioAgent.serve` processes one line at a time, so while `_prompt` is running inside `handle`, the next input line is not read. Given a client that sends `session/prompt` and, while `on_prompt` is still working, sends `session/cancel`, the cancel notification sits unread until `on_prompt` returns; `session.cancelled` is never set during the prompt, so the prompt finishes normally instead of returning `"cancelled"`. The same flag is sticky: the late cancel line is then read after the prompt has already been answered, sets `session.cancelled = True`, and because `_prompt` only reads and clears that flag after the next `on_prompt` call, that stale cancel then causes the next prompt to be reported as `"cancelled"` even though no cancel was sent for it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py AcpStdioAgent.handle / AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s stated conformance requirement says “unavailable is never passed”, but this fake explicitly passes `A.UNAVAILABLE` to callers. `FakeAcpClient(mode="unavailable").connect(1.0)` returns an `A.AcpHandshake` with status `A.UNAVAILABLE`; `new_session` and `prompt` also return `A.UNAVAILABLE` when `connect` was not called first. This lets a consumer using the fake observe the exact status the port must never pass, so the fake violates the stated contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py FakeAcpClient.connect/new_session/prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpAgent()` is called with no arguments, but every other construction in the file passes a `Script` (`FakeAcpAgent(SCRIPT)` or `FakeAcpAgent(SCRIPT, agent_info=...)`), and the change intent describes the fake as “replays a scripted session.” If `FakeAcpAgent.__init__` requires a script (there is no no-arg constructor visible in this use), this line raises `TypeError`, so the test cannot pass; it should be `FakeAcpAgent(SCRIPT)`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:test_the_adapter_and_the_fake_satisfy_the_ports

chunk_findings.detail: The `lane_event` function accesses `.get("content")` on an unvalidated update dictionary and immediately calls `.get("text")` on it without verifying that `content` is actually a dictionary. If `content` is a non-dict object (e.g., a list or a primitive), an `AttributeError` will be raised when `content.get` is evaluated, crashing the adapter event handler when processing malformed or unexpected ACP stream updates. Given input where `update` contains `{"sessionUpdate": "agent_message_chunk", "content": "just-a-string"}`, `lane_event` raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:127

chunk_findings.detail: `serve` reads one frame and calls `handle` synchronously, and `handle` for `session/prompt` blocks inside `_on_prompt` until the turn returns. Therefore a `session/cancel` notification sent after the prompt request is not read or processed while the prompt is active. If `on_prompt` follows the documented cancellation contract and loops on `session.cancelled` (for example `while not session.cancelled: emit(...)`), the flag is never set because the serve loop is stuck in `_prompt`; the agent deadlocks or ignores the cancel. Given initialize, `session/new`, a `session/prompt` frame, then a `session/cancel` frame, the cancel is never handled during the active prompt, so the agent-side cancel capability is non-functional. [D-acp-r2]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent.serve

chunk_findings.detail: `_prompt` does not inspect or clear `session.cancelled` before starting a turn; it always calls `_on_prompt`, then reads the flag. A cancel notification that arrived while no prompt was active (including a request-shaped cancel that `handle` rejects but still applies) therefore makes the next prompt execute side effects and emit updates, then return `{"stopReason":"cancelled"}`. For example: after `session/new` creates `s1`, send `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":"s1"}}`, then send `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/prompt","params":{"sessionId":"s1","prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"go"}]}}` with an `on_prompt` that records the call and returns `"end_turn"`. The recorded call proves the turn ran, but the response is cancelled. The added `cancelled, session.cancelled = session.cancelled, False` only consumes one stale flag after the turn, so the earlier cancel-lifecycle defect remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `_on_other` assumes `params` is a dict. During a prompt, a parseable but malformed non-response frame such as `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":["x"]}` reaches `seen`; `msg.get("params") or {}` yields the truthy list `["x"]`, and the next `params.get("update")` raises `AttributeError`, so `prompt` crashes instead of returning a bounded outcome. The same applies to a malformed `session/request_permission` with array or string `params`. The server half explicitly guards `session/cancel` with `isinstance(params, dict)`, so the client half should not crash on malformed but parseable wire frames.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._on_other

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpClient.prompt` iterates over every entry in `self.agent.script.asks` unconditionally. When a permission policy denies an ask, lines 178-179 set `result.stop_reason = A.CANCELLED`, but the loop does not break. Given `Script(asks=[{"toolCall": {"title": "edit1"}}, {"toolCall": {"title": "edit2"}}])` and a call such as `client.prompt(sid, "x", 1, permission=lambda ask: None)`, the permission callback is invoked for `edit2` after the turn has already been cancelled by `edit1`, and `result.permissions` contains two entries. A denied permission should stop the turn and prevent further permission-policy side effects.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:174

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpAgent._prompt` streams all scripted events before it considers `session.cancelled`. After `client.cancel(session_id)`, the next `client.prompt(session_id, ...)` returns `stop_reason == A.CANCELLED`, but lines 87-89 still append the full scripted update sequence to `agent.sent`, so `FakeAcpClient.prompt` maps those updates and calls `on_event` for them. For example, with `Script(events=[{"type": "agent_message_chunk", "content": {"type": "text", "text": "hi"}}])`, a prompt following a cancel still delivers the chunk even though the prompt result is cancelled. If a cancel ends the turn, the cancelled turn should not emit the scripted updates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:87

chunk_findings.detail: The new docs codify a cancel model that cannot honor `session/cancel` for the active prompt over the normal stdio transport, and it also lets an idle cancel affect a later prompt. It states that `AcpStdioAgent.serve` reads one frame at a time, so a cancel is seen between turns, and that a caller that needs to interrupt a running turn must feed frames from a second thread while `on_prompt` watches `session.cancelled`. Given a client using `serve`, sending `initialize`, `session/new`, then `session/prompt` while `on_prompt` waits for cancellation, and sending `{"method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":"s1"}}` on stdin, the documented `serve` loop is blocked inside `handle(session/prompt)` and will not process the cancel until the prompt has already finished; the prompt therefore cannot stop with `cancelled` as required. Conversely, if `session/cancel` is sent while no prompt is active, the docs say the next prompt reports `cancelled`, so a stale/idle cancel cancels an unrelated new prompt. This contradicts the intended ACP cancel behavior [D-acp-r2].
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/acp.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: The `_Peer` permission-answer path assumes the client’s `session/request_permission` reply is double-wrapped as `{"result": {"outcome": {"outcome": ...}}}`. If the client returns the conforming ACP shape described in the earlier [D-acp-r2] finding — e.g. `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"ask-1","result":{"outcome":"selected","optionId":"yes"}}` — then `mid, outcome = self.asking, msg["result"]["outcome"]` binds `outcome` to the string `"selected"`, and the next line `outcome.get("outcome")` raises `AttributeError`. Thus `_client_cases` fails/hangs against a corrected client and only passes if the adapter still emits the previously reported non-conforming `{"outcome": {"outcome": ...}}` double-wrap.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:_Peer.send

chunk_findings.detail: These tests still encode a cancel that arrives with no active prompt as cancellation of the next prompt. `test_the_agent_streams_updates_and_keeps_the_injected_mcp_servers` sends `session/cancel` after `session/prompt` has already completed and asserts `agent.sessions[sid].cancelled is True`; `test_a_cancel_during_a_prompt_makes_the_stop_reason_cancelled` shows that any prompt started while `sessions[sid].cancelled` is true returns `{"stopReason": "cancelled"}` even when `_on_prompt` returns `end_turn`. Therefore the sequence `session/new`, `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/prompt` (with an `on_prompt` that returns `end_turn`) cancels the second prompt, although a cancel with no active turn should be a no-op. Clearing the flag only after the next prompt does not answer the earlier sticky-cancel defect.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:test_the_agent_streams_updates_and_keeps_the_injected_mcp_servers

chunk_findings.detail: The `session/request_permission` response is double-wrapped. `outcome` is already the ACP result object (`{"outcome": "selected", "optionId": chosen}` or `{"outcome": "cancelled"}`), but the code sends `ok(msg["id"], {"outcome": outcome})`, producing `"result": {"outcome": {"outcome": "selected", ...}}`. A conforming agent expects `"result": {"outcome": "selected", ...}` and cannot parse the reply, so a permission request during `prompt` fails or hangs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._on_other

chunk_findings.detail: `serve` feeds one line at a time to `handle`, and `handle("session/prompt")` blocks inside `_on_prompt`; a `session/cancel` frame sent while the turn is running is not read until `_on_prompt` returns. An `on_prompt` that runs until cancellation, as the `OnPrompt` contract implies, deadlocks instead of stopping, so the advertised cancel-during-prompt cannot work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent.serve

chunk_findings.detail: `session.cancelled` is set by any `session/cancel` and is not reset at the start of a new prompt; it is only cleared after `_on_prompt`. After creating a session, send `session/cancel` while no prompt is active, then `session/prompt` with `_on_prompt` returning `"end_turn"`; the code captures the stale `True` and returns `{"stopReason": "cancelled"}`. A cancel with no active turn poisons the next turn.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `_on_other` assumes `params` is a dict for `session/update` and `session/request_permission`. A parseable non-object params from the agent, e.g. `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":["x"]}` while a prompt is pending, makes `(msg.get("params") or {}).get("update")` call `.get` on a list and raise `AttributeError`, aborting the prompt instead of ignoring or rejecting the malformed frame.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._on_other

chunk_findings.detail: In the non-result branch, `return done(ERROR, error=msg["error"] if isinstance(msg["error"], dict) else {})` evaluates `msg["error"]` before the conditional has established the key exists. A JSON-RPC frame with the matching id but neither `result` nor `error` (for example `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}`) raises `KeyError: 'error'` instead of returning an `Outcome`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._exchange

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpClient._ask` returns an error outcome without a `result`: when the fake agent replies with a JSON-RPC error (for example `session/prompt` for an unknown session), line 127 constructs `A.Outcome(A.ERROR, error=reply["error"])`. Every caller then dereferences `out.result` as a dict: `connect` line 138 (`out.result.get("agentInfo")`), `new_session` line 151 (`out.result.get("sessionId")`), and `prompt` line 168 (`out.result.get("stopReason", "")`). Given `client.connect(1.0)` followed by `client.prompt("no-such-session", "hi", 1.0)`, the error outcome has no dict result, so this crashes on `.get` (or when constructing `A.Outcome` if `result` has no default) instead of returning an `A.PromptResult`/`A.AcpSession` with `status == A.ERROR`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:127

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpAgent.handle` handles `session/cancel` before the `"id" not in msg` check and before `A.check_request`, then returns `None` unconditionally. A JSON-RPC request carrying an id, such as `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":"s1"}}`, therefore gets no response; a JSON-RPC client would wait forever, and `FakeAcpClient._ask` asserts that the reply is not `None`. If `session/cancel` is notification-only, this id-bearing message is invalid and should be rejected by `A.check_request`; if it may be a request, it must be answered. Returning `None` is wrong for any id-bearing cancel message.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The new documentation defines `session/cancel` as not cancelling the active turn: “`session/cancel` marks the session, and the NEXT turn that finishes reports `cancelled` once”, and then says `AcpStdioAgent.serve` only sees a cancel between turns. ACP’s `session/cancel` is meant to cancel the in-flight `session/prompt`, so with a long-running `on_prompt` a client that sends `session/prompt` then `session/cancel` will, per this doc, get the normal `stopReason` when the task completes, not `cancelled`. The suggested workaround (“feeds frames from a second thread and watches `session.cancelled` inside `on_prompt`”) is caller-invented and not part of the adapter’s public contract, so the documented behavior defeats the stated intent that the port supports cancellation. This is the same `serve`/blocking defect as previous finding #8, now enshrined in the docs rather than fixed.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/acp.md:13

chunk_findings.detail: `_Peer.send` assumes the client’s answer to `session/request_permission` is double-wrapped: it executes `msg["result"]["outcome"]` and then calls `.get("outcome")` on that value. A correct JSON-RPC result for a selected permission ask is a single-level ACP result such as `{"outcome": "selected", "optionId": "yes"}`; in that case `msg["result"]["outcome"]` is the string `"selected"`, so line 58 raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'`. This makes the default-client conformance case fail once the client sends the correct wire shape, and only passes while `AcpStdioClient` emits the double-wrapped result this test should catch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:56-58
